answer: Behavioral-fingerprint escrow unlock blocks sybil attacks by tying each identity to a work pattern. A new agent posts a 50 POA deposit and works three epochs; timing, task mix and peer contacts form its fingerprint, and only a fingerprint consistent across all three epochs unlocks the deposit and voting weight. Forging 100 identities costs 5,000 POA locked and 300 epoch-units of work, while an honest agent pays 50 POA once. A falcon cannot hunt two ridges at once, and no operator can run a hundred distinct fingerprints. The velvet side: honest agents get the deposit back, rewards undiluted.
